clue.text: I won't go on the big swings for now

indicators.note: something that swings moves to and fro, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.words: I won't go on the big
parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A timid child at the playground declares they will stay off the big swings, at least for the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swings' looks like the playground equipment completing the sentence; it is the shuffle signal, acting on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sufficient for the time being, an exact equivalent of the temporary sense of the definition.

clue.text: Book that reveals the origins of Kurtz's nativism?

parts.words: Book that reveals the origins of Kurtz's nativism?
parts.note: surface reading: a novel explaining where the character Kurtz's native prejudices came from
setter's reading: the opening letters of Kurtz and nativism are K and N, the two central letters of the word darkness

explanation.surface: A literary critic asks which novel explains where the character Kurtz's xenophobia began.
explanation.walkthrough: Kurtz is the ivory trader in Conrad's novella, so the surface fits; but read literally, K and N sit at the heart of the word DARKNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad's novella of 1899 is a famous book, and Kurtz is its central figure.

clue.text: Excessive coverage about king shielded by conspicuous wealth

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: something shielded is protected by a covering, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: showy richness
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A media critic complains that a monarch is hidden behind too much reporting and lavish display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' suggests news reporting, but here it is flesh covering the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulence is fatness, a body carrying too much padding of flesh, hence an excessive covering.

clue.text: Prevent doctor taking care of adult as a temporary measure

parts.note: to prevent is to stop

indicators.note: taking care of someone means looking after them closely, so one part holds the other within it

parts.note: a general practitioner, the British family doctor
A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A health service manager blocks a doctor from treating a grown-up patient, as a short-term fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a makeshift that fills a need until something permanent arrives.

clue.text: Go round

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attempt, as in 'have a go'
second meaning: a single round of ammunition fired

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a single instruction to circle something; they are separate nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a try at something and a discharged bullet or cartridge.

clue.text: Over time, he treated them badly with many offensive items?

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of someone who, over the years, mistreated people while carrying plenty of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' suggests rudeness, but it means weapons of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone armed to the teeth carries a great many weapons, which are offensive items in the military sense.

clue.text: Ancient ground is all she had lost

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old piece of land was the only thing a woman lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun for land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something extremely old, so it is a colourful synonym for very old.

clue.text: Retired auditor's uncertainty about branch?

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so we take what is heard rather than what is written

parts.note: a doubt concerning a bough, a tree branch, said out loud

explanation.surface: An accountant's hesitation over a company's branch office, as he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' and 'branch' suggest accounts and a bank branch; the auditor is just a hearer and the branch is a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow out is to withdraw or retire gracefully, so the past tense matches 'Retired'.

clue.text: Present case for scholarly dissent

parts.note: present in the sense of in attendance

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of the next word are used

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: An academic offering an argument for disagreeing with scholarly consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present case' reads as making an argument; 'Present' alone is HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is dissent from established, especially religious, doctrine.

clue.text: Argue about pressure to get ready

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around, so the letters of the word are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: People squabble about the pressure they face to be prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: To gear up is to prepare oneself or equip for something coming, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Drug ring close to dodgy corporation

parts.note: slang for cannabis
to ring someone is to give them a bell, British slang for a phone call

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: A drugs gang operating near a shady company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a firm; it is an old jocular word for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a dated humorous term for a paunch, and a potbelly is a protruding stomach.

clue.text: Derelict house with deficient facilities

indicators.note: deficient means lacking something, so the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
British slang for a toilet; 'the facilities' is a euphemism for the lavatory

explanation.surface: An abandoned house with poor plumbing and amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derelict' looks like an adjective describing the house; it is the noun for a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict, as a noun, is a homeless destitute person, and a hobo is an American word for a tramp.

clue.text: Corrupt chief when serving board

parts.note: lead as an adjective, main
as in 'as I arrived'
a flat board for carrying food

explanation.surface: A company boss gets corrupted while sitting on a board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving board' suggests sitting on a company board; it is a tea tray.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead astray is to tempt someone into wrongdoing, so it is a verb synonym of corrupt.

clue.text: Emotional detachment of American people consuming fake news?

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one part ends up inside another

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a people as a nation
a falsehood

explanation.surface: Americans feel emotionally cut off because their society is swallowing misinformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the feeling of being estranged or isolated from others, a state of emotional distance.

clue.text: Bland answer and negative response deny breaking up

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: breaking up means falling apart, so the letters of the word are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: a refusal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dull answer and a flat refusal, denying that a relationship is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking up' suggests a romance ending; it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means inoffensive and unlikely to provoke, so it is a synonym of bland.

clue.text: Rule international court is constrained by another

indicators.note: something constrained is held inside limits, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: another word for court, as in to court or date someone
I is the abbreviation for international
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A world court finds its power to rule limited by a rival court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another word for court; here court as a verb, to woo or date.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to lay down the law or command, a verb synonym of rule.

clue.text: Poetic movement's message largely accepted by spiritual leader

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the first part goes inside the second

parts.note: a Muslim prayer leader

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the gist is the core message

explanation.surface: A movement's core teaching is approved by its spiritual head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetic movement's' has the definition carry the 's, read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagism was an early twentieth-century school of poetry, led by Pound, favouring precise images.

clue.text: Newly arrived Australian staff guarding vessel for experienced worker

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround and protect it, so one part encloses another

parts.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, a newborn Australian
a pot or vase
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A recent immigrant to Australia is hired to guard a ship, for a seasoned tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly arrived' suggests an immigrant; it is a newborn animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman who has served an apprenticeship, a reliable experienced worker.

clue.text: Inspects entrances for sewers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: looks over closely, a verb
second meaning: the holes in needles through which those who sew pass thread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, so the entrances seem to be manholes; read it as people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for looking at and a plural noun for the threading holes of needles.

clue.text: Worries about including child's final appearance

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one part goes inside the other
about suggests turning round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: worries in the sense of gnaws at
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A parent frets over their child's last performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after child is the link 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a final performance or act before retirement, from the legend that swans sing before dying.

clue.text: Get rid of piece of superfluous text

indicators.note: a piece is only part of the whole, so the letters run inside the following words

parts.note: sits across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: An editor wants to delete an unnecessary passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust is to remove or expel someone or something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Article is defending singular argument

indicators.note: defending means shielding on either side, so the pair surround the next letter

parts.note: the definite article
taken as written
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A newspaper article stands up for one unusual line of reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article is' must be taken as a pair of pieces that together flank the singular letter, not as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward and argued for, so it is an argument in that sense.

clue.text: Secret police start to subvert stable state

parts.note: the East German state security service

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A secret police force begins to undermine a settled regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a nation the police are undermining; it means a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium or inactivity where nothing changes.

clue.text: Firm debate is bound to stop hunt

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one part is pushed inside another

parts.note: to stalk prey is to hunt it
a bound is a leap or hop

explanation.surface: A company's discussion is certain to halt a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', as in 'is bound to'; it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop talk is conversation about one's work, so a discussion of a firm's business qualifies.
